Technical Analysis: Starfish TS Splicer Reduces Latency and Enhances Signal Integrity with Latest Release

At the recent NAB Show, Starfish announced the release of its latest Transport Stream (TS) Splicer, a software-based solution designed to enable frame-accurate splicing of MPEG-TS streams. This technology is particularly relevant for broadcast engineers and CTOs, as it has the potential to significantly reduce latency and improve signal integrity in live signal transport applications. The TS Splicer is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast infrastructure.

Operational ROI

The Starfish TS Splicer offers significant operational benefits for broadcast engineers, particularly in terms of reduced transmission costs and lower latency compared to traditional satellite or fibre-based transmission methods. By enabling frame-accurate splicing of MPEG-TS streams, the TS Splicer can reduce the need for costly and complex signal routing infrastructure, resulting in a more streamlined and efficient workflow. For example, in a typical live production scenario, the TS Splicer can reduce latency by up to 50% compared to traditional methods, resulting in a more responsive and engaging viewer experience.

In comparison to existing approaches, the Starfish TS Splicer offers a more flexible and scalable solution for live signal transport. Traditional methods often rely on hardware-based solutions, which can be inflexible and prone to signal degradation. In contrast, the TS Splicer is a software-based solution that can be easily integrated with existing infrastructure, reducing the need for costly hardware upgrades and minimizing the risk of signal degradation. Additionally, the TS Splicer supports a range of industry-standard protocols, including SRT, RIST, and AES67, ensuring compatibility with a wide range of broadcast equipment and systems.

Security & Integration

The Starfish TS Splicer is designed to integrate seamlessly with existing broadcast IT stacks, supporting a range of industry-standard protocols and compliance requirements. The solution is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, ensuring compatibility with other ST 2110-compliant devices and systems. Additionally, the TS Splicer supports the NMOS IS-04 protocol, enabling easy integration with other NMOS-compliant devices and systems. In terms of cybersecurity, the TS Splicer features robust security measures, including encryption and secure authentication, to ensure the integrity and security of live signals. The solution also supports the use of JPEG XS compression, which provides a high-quality and low-latency compression format for live signal transport.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The Starfish TS Splicer requires a minimum of 10GbE network bandwidth and a quad-core processor to ensure optimal performance. Additionally, the solution is compatible with a range of operating systems, including Windows and Linux.
  • Compatibility: The TS Splicer is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-20 standard and supports the NMOS IS-04 protocol, ensuring compatibility with a wide range of broadcast equipment and systems. The solution also supports the SRT and RIST protocols, enabling easy integration with other SRT and RIST-compliant devices and systems.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new features and enhancements for live signal transport and latency reduction. Additionally, the development of new compression formats, such as JPEG XS, is expected to have a significant impact on the broadcast industry, enabling higher-quality and lower-latency live signal transport.

The release of the Starfish TS Splicer signals a significant shift in the broadcast industry towards more flexible and scalable live signal transport solutions. As the industry continues to evolve, engineering teams should prioritize the development of software-based solutions that can integrate seamlessly with existing infrastructure, while also reducing latency and improving signal integrity. By adopting solutions like the Starfish TS Splicer, broadcast engineers can ensure a more efficient and responsive workflow, resulting in a better viewer experience.

Analysis: Starfish's TS Splicer supports ST 2110, enabling efficient IP-based video switching with low latency and precise bitrate control, suitable for live broadcast and streaming workflows.
